rationale: The requested objective is step_ms (max across ranks; original baseline 136.86/137.05 ms). Composition of one accumulated step, from measured evidence: non-NCCL compute kernels total ~34.0 ms for all 4 micro-batches (nsys rank-0 trace spans the complete accumulate: 8 embedding gathers, 13 NCCL kernels, ends at the loss stack), while the 13 DDP bucket allreduces cost ~61.8 ms when measured cleanly (collective_calibration: 28,351,488 B -> 3.52 ms median, 157,541,376 B -> 19.50 ms; 12x3.52+19.5). Exposure: after the first collective kernel starts, only 8.49 ms of compute remains in the final backward and 1.73 ms after the last starts, so communication is essentially fully serialized at the step tail; overlap with compute cannot be increased further inside the frozen no_sync schedule. The wire path is NCCL RING_LL over SHM/direct (peer_access 0 in both directions, NVLink unsupported, 2 channels) at a logical 8.05 GB/s for both payload sizes, while device telemetry during the comm window shows pcie.tx ~7.3 GB/s and pcie.rx ~8.5 GB/s, i.e. the LL-protocol path, not the link, appears to set the ~62 ms floor (PCIe/SHM saturation estimate for the 497,759,232 B per-rank gradient payload is ~40 ms). These 13 collectives are the only collectives in the step (payload coverage 13/13 observed) and are jointly owned by exactly two eligible call groups at the shared c10d.allreduce_.default dispatch boundary: f833b57a373d8262a384 (call d0938de87369efd500322679, 12 invocations of the 7,087,872-element bucket shape) and 8525af72c631b94e3dd0 (call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b, the single 39,385,344-element embedding bucket). Bucket membership spreads across all layer groups, so no per-layer group independently owns communication cost; conversely, faster local compute kernels (mm 10.5 ms, addmm 4.8 ms inclusive) cannot move step_ms materially while ~45% of the step is exposed communication. A replacement must cover both payload shapes at this one boundary, so the two groups are selected as a joint candidate. Constraints preserved: same worker-initialized process group, async_op=True Work semantics, in-place float32 SUM into the gradient_as_bucket_view bucket tensors, no DDP configuration/bucketing change and no comm hook; DDP's own world-size division and the frozen step boundary stay untouched. Per-element the reduction remains a single two-addend sum (commutative), so results are bitwise identical to NCCL's ring sum, keeping the exact cross-rank replica check (atol=0/rtol=0), the full-global-batch gradient reference check and the parameter check unchanged, and the diagnostic communication goal only improves.
hypothesis: Replacing the bucket allreduce dispatch at both selected call groups with a bandwidth-optimized two-rank reduction on the existing NCCL process group - e.g. a chunked one-shot exchange that splits each bucket into large contiguous halves, exchanges them with point-to-point sends/receceptions so both directions move SIMPLE-protocol bulk transfers, adds each half locally, and swaps the reduced halves back into the bucket view; or any equivalent path that lifts effective throughput above the observed 8.05 GB/s RING_LL ceiling - will shorten the ~62 ms serialized tail communication toward the ~40 ms link-saturation estimate and reduce step_ms by roughly 10-20 ms (~8-15%), because communication is measured to be almost fully exposed (only 8.49 ms of overlap available) and is the largest single block of the 137 ms step. Bitwise-identical gradient values (two-addend commutative sum, DDP still divides by world size) preserve every quality check including exact cross-rank equality. This is a hypothesis to be tested: if the 8 GB/s LL result already reflects the SHM/PCIe hard ceiling for this pair, or if chunking adds launch overhead comparable to the bandwidth gain, measured step_ms will not improve and the candidate must be rejected on measurement; expected benefit is not acceptance.
